column3: "enforces the battle lines". the main frontline, enforcers mark where each team should be in a fight and are the ones to start it. they create the space for the rest of their team to capitalize
"duel opponents". duelists main job is to pick their target and kill it. they can do this either supported by their team, or alone. excel at 1v1

"control the enemy's options". either via debuffs, taxing, crowd control, area damage, or any other means, the job of a controller is to dictate what the opponent can and can't do, while sometimes giving support to their own team

"fixes the match in their favour". a fixer can come in many shapes and sizes. either not proficient in combat but with an arsenal of supporting utility, or increasing board presence, they provide serious value to a win
focused on protecting either itself or teammates. wants to survive a lot. not the best at progressing the frontline, but great at holding it
wants to do a lot of damage with a lot of health. somewhat individualistic. advances the frontline by killing the enemies frontline
wants to get in behind the enemies frontline, and then crunch it with the rest of its team. high movement, and some survivability
plays mainly in the frontline supporting the enforcers by pressuring the enemies frontline. can both create scraps (put enemies low) or take scraps (kill low enemis)
plays further away from the team, can either be VERY long range, VERY close range, or in between. wants to take scraps, or just one shot enemies even
can play with the pack, go alone, or go with another ally, has very high movement and escapability. wants to create scraps
controls by denying the enemy team's options. can deny space, normally use structures, or have stuns
controls by weaking the enemy team. has a lot of debuffs, or board manipulation tools
controls by punishing the enemy team. great at area and crowd control, either by damaging an area or doing other stuff.
they create the advantage for their team by having more entities on the board than the opponents via creating them, and giving the team more options
have loads of utility, mainly utility to help the team and not debuff the opponents, be it buffs, movement option or action economy
their main goal is to have allies not die. they can heal them, prevent damage, help them escape, the main goal is to ensure the team is kept in a fight
